questions.q: What does SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA do that SYSTEM$CLASSIFY (applied to one table) does not?
options: Classifies and optionally auto-tags every table inside a named schema in one call
Deletes tags from every table in a schema
Applies a masking policy directly to every column in a schema
Only works on system tags, never custom tags
questions.explain: SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA runs the classification engine against every table in the named schema in a single call, rather than requiring one call per table.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why did the FRANCHISE table end up tagged even though it was never named directly in the SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA call?
options: Because it is a table inside the raw_pos schema that the call targeted
Because FRANCHISE shares a primary key with a table that was named
Because every Snowflake account tags FRANCHISE by default
It was a data entry error — FRANCHISE should not have been tagged
questions.explain: SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA propagates to every table inside the targeted schema, not just tables explicitly named — FRANCHISE was tagged purely by virtue of being inside raw_pos.

questions.q: Does CREATE TABLE ... CLONE copy the source table's tags to the new clone?
options: No — tags are not automatically copied; they must be reapplied explicitly if needed
Yes, tags and any attached masking policy transfer automatically
Only system tags are copied, custom tags are not
Only if the clone is created in the same schema as the source
questions.explain: CREATE TABLE ... CLONE (and ... LIKE) do not automatically copy tags from the source object — a clone's columns start untagged even if the source's columns carry PII tags.

questions.q: What is the practical risk created by the clone tag-copying behavior described in this lesson?
options: A clone of a table with sensitive data can sit completely unprotected by tag-driven masking unless tags are reapplied by hand
Clones cannot be queried until tags are manually applied
Cloning a table automatically deletes the source table's tags too
Clones always inherit a stricter masking policy than their source
questions.explain: Because the clone doesn't inherit the source's tags, it also doesn't inherit any masking policy bound to those tags via ALTER TAG — leaving sensitive data in the clone unprotected unless someone reapplies the tags.

questions.q: How does a tag-driven masking policy on a base table reach a downstream view built on that table?
options: It propagates forward through the dependency graph automatically, with no separate configuration on the view
The view must have the same masking policy manually reattached to its own columns
It only reaches the view if SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA is also run against the view's schema
Views never inherit masking policies from base tables under any circumstances
questions.explain: Because the tag (and its attached policy) lives on the base table's columns, any view selecting from those columns inherits the protection automatically through the dependency graph.
